proposals.announcement_evidence: was awarded a $34,810,595 firm-fixed-price contract for wireless AT platform test sets
proposals.lexicon_quote: tems (NGATS), 930 Maintenance Support Devices (MSD) and 280 Wireless At-Platform Test Sets (WATS) to support Base requirements and test and diagnostic equipm
proposals.rationale: The announcement's item of supply is the named end item of this procurement line, not a platform the contract merely supports: BLI 0200MB4000 (Integrated Family Of Test Equipment) owns the name 'Wireless At-Platform Test Sets (WATS)' in its own narrative, which states the line buys 280 WATS alongside NGATS and MSD. The announcement's phrase 'wireless AT platform test sets' is the same name with the hyphen and capitalisation dropped by the defense.gov copy desk (which is why the deterministic verbatim pass missed it and the record landed in the residue), so this is an alias of the lexicon name rather than a coincidental English phrase. The award is a firm-fixed-price production buy of that hardware placed by Army Contracting Command, Redstone Arsenal, against an existing contract - a procurement action against a procurement line, with no O&M sustainment or services framing anywhere in the paragraph. No other PE in this org's index carries the WATS name.

refute_a.reason: Survives lens A: the award's item of supply IS this line's own work, not a platform it supports - BLI 0200MB4000 (Integrated Family Of Test Equipment) is an Other Procurement, Army line whose own narrative procures 280 Wireless At-Platform Test Sets (WATS), and the announcement is a firm-fixed-price supply action for exactly that hardware placed by Army Contracting Command, Redstone Arsenal, with no O&M, sustainment, engineering-support or services framing anywhere in the paragraph; the announcement states no appropriation at all ('funding will be determined with each order'), so nothing in the text contradicts the line's procurement color, and the ordering-vehicle shape is not the section 3 IDIQ-umbrella reject because the vehicle names one program item rather than no program; IFTE is a named program of record with enumerated members (IFTE, MSD, NGATS, WATS), not a rollup or catch-all, and its title does not trip CATCHALL_TITLE.

refute_b.reason: Alias is real, not invented: A.tsv line 29 carries 'Wireless At-Platform Test Sets (WATS)' under 0200MB4000/doc 346 verbatim, and the lexicon quote is verbatim from that entry; the announcement's 'wireless AT platform test sets' is the same name with hyphen/case dropped, not an English phrase. No other PE in the org A index owns the WATS name (the only other test-equipment lines, 0605G02510 TEMOD and 6500GA0750, own CALSETS/CTE/GPETE/RTS and DSESTS - different named sets). The one genuine collision is outside the index: RDT&E PE 0604746A also owns 'Wireless At-platform Test Set (WATS)', but its narrative develops next-gen MSD and 'supporting capability enhancement of' WATS, while this record is a competitively solicited (five bids) firm-fixed-price buy of the sets themselves by ACC-Redstone - that evidence does not link there equally well, and 0604746A carries no doc_id so it is not proposable in any case. No variant/increment mismatch and the evidence is the item of supply, not the contractor name.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for modification of 49 Bradley Fighting Vehicles from the M3A2 version to the M2A2 version and 49 final inspection records
proposals.lexicon_quote: The Bradley Program (MOD) funding line procures upgrades to the Bradley Fighting Vehicle
proposals.rationale: This is not a contract that merely supports the Bradley platform - it physically reconfigures 49 already-fielded Bradley Fighting Vehicles from the M3A2 cavalry variant to the M2A2 infantry variant, which is exactly the work BLI 1678GZ2400's own narrative describes ('The Bradley Program (MOD) funding line procures upgrades to the Bradley Fighting Vehicle'). The vehicle name the announcement uses is the same org's own lexicon name under this BLI ('The Bradley Fighting Vehicle (BFV)'), and the modification framing is what ties the action to the MOD line rather than to a base procurement or an RDT&E line. The action is a modification to a TACOM firm-fixed-price basic contract with BAE Systems Land and Armaments at York, Pennsylvania, the Bradley production house, and is funded with fiscal 2014 procurement dollars, so it is a procurement action against a procurement line. The one soft spot lens A should test is that the paragraph writes the appropriation as 'other procurement funds' where Bradley modifications sit in Procurement of Weapons and Tracked Combat Vehicles; the vehicle-conversion work itself is unambiguously this line's own.

refute_a.reason: Refuted on money color, the lens A ground the proposal itself flagged: the announcement obligates 'Fiscal 2014 other procurement funds' - Other Procurement, Army - while BLI 1678GZ2400 Bradley Program (MOD) sits in Procurement of Weapons and Tracked Combat Vehicles, Army (data/research/jbook_line_universe.json accounts: 'Procurement of W&TCV, Army'), so the only appropriation the announcement names is disjoint from this line's; the M3A2-to-M2A2 conversion work does match the MOD line's mission and the vehicle name is this BLI's own lexicon name, but the claim being published is that this action paid for THIS line's work, and the award's stated money color points at a different account, which is the exact failure mode the 2026-09-04 held-out study found - on a 2014 PIID whose lake-side funding accounts are likely NULL, money_color_ok() would treat the color as unknown and publish, so this lens is the only guard, and the rubric's default is to refute.

refute_b.reason: Name and quote are real: A.tsv line 895 'The Bradley Program (MOD)' / 1678GZ2400 / doc 350 matches the index row verbatim and the lexicon quote is verbatim. The Bradley name collisions in the index all resolve away from the alternatives: 1382GZ3300 owns only fire-support names (Bradley Fire Support Team (BFIST), Bradley Common Display, FS3) and this paragraph names no fire-support role - its stated end state is the plain M2A2 infantry variant, not an M7/BFIST; 0604802A and 2650E08200 own only the 25mm BADGER cartridge names, and 2650E08200's 'Bradley Fighting Vehicle (BFV)' lexicon entry is ownership='mentioned' (platform reference) and is correctly absent from the index. Within the index the BFV name and the MOD line belong to 1678GZ2400 alone. The M3A2-to-M2A2 conversion is a whole-vehicle reconfiguration of the named platform, so it is not a different variant's program but this line's own modification work; the evidence is the work description, not the BAE name. The FY2014 action against a modern-J-book narrative is inherent to the method rather than specific to this record, and the 'other procurement funds' wording is lens A's appropriation question, not an identity one.

proposals.announcement_evidence: offsite technical support to the National Ground Intelligence Center
proposals.lexicon_quote: Acquisition and exploitation are executed according to Army Foreign Materiel Program (FMP) Plan prioritization and with the approval of the Army Deputy
proposals.rationale: The described work - analysing and exploiting foreign military hardware for scientific and technical intelligence - is a close description of PE 0605709A ('Exploitation of Foreign Items'), whose lexicon name is the Army Foreign Materiel Program, and NGIC is the Army element that executes that program. But the announcement names an organisation (the National Ground Intelligence Center's foreign materiel directorate), not the program, so nothing in the text is the program name or a designator variant of it; and the vehicle is a cost-plus-fixed-fee IDIQ for 'offsite technical support' whose performance locations and funding are explicitly 'determined with each order', so no appropriation is stated and no dollar in the paragraph can be tied to this program element's own work. Under the rubric's evidence standard that is a support-services ceiling described by mission rather than an award that funds this line, and the project publishes the smaller true number, so this does not reach link.

proposals.announcement_evidence: UH-72 Lakota contractor logistics support parts support and sustainment additional flying hours
proposals.rationale: The name matches this org's index row exactly (UH-72 Lakota), and Airbus Helicopters is the program's prime, so the identity is not in doubt. What fails is the attribution: BLI 4742A05001 is the aircraft procurement line that buys Lakotas, while this modification buys contractor logistics support, parts support, sustainment and additional flying hours with fiscal 2017 operations and maintenance (Army) funds. That is the exact failure mode the rubric's lens A names - O&M sustainment attached to a procurement line - so the award pays for keeping fielded aircraft flying, not for this program element's own work. Name present, evidence short of the standard: weak, not link.

proposals.program_name: Modular Fuel System (MFS) Tank Rack Module (TRM) - M107 40gpm Pump Modification Kit

proposals.lexicon_quote: Modular Fuel System (MFS) Tank Rack Module (TRM) - M107 40gpm Pump Modification Kit
proposals.rationale: 'Tank rack module' appears inside this index row's name, and the Modular Fuel System TRM is plausibly the same item the award produces. But the row names a specific M107 40gpm pump modification kit, not TRM production, and PE 0604804A is an RDT&E engineering-development line (Logistics and Engineer Equipment - Eng Dev) while this is a firm-fixed-price production order placed by Army Contracting Command, Detroit Arsenal, with work locations and funding determined per order. A production buy cannot fund an engineering-development program element's own work, and the announcement gives no appropriation to test that with, so the fragment name match does not meet the evidence standard.

proposals.lexicon_quote: l be used to purchase 44 SGT STOUT systems, retrofit single Stinger Vehicle Universal Launcher (SVUL) systems to dual SVUL, initial spares, software maintenance,

proposals.announcement_evidence: maintenance and training on the Counter-Rocket Artillery Mortar, Counter-Unmanned Aerial System, command and control system
proposals.rationale: Rejected on two of the rubric's patterns at once. First, the work is maintenance and training - generic services - funded with fiscal 2018 operations and maintenance Army funds, so nothing here pays for a procurement or development line's own content. Second, the identity does not hold: the announcement names the C-RAM / Counter-UAS command and control system (the fire-control C2 that Northrop Grumman sustains), whereas the index name is the Counter-Small Unmanned Aerial System program, a distinct later program; and three separate rows in this org's index carry a C-sUAS name (0010I24000, 0219AD0500 and 0604531A), so the name does not resolve to a single owner even if the scope matched.

proposals.program_name: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) / Intel Surv Recon (ISR)
proposals.announcement_evidence: research, development, test and evaluation support to intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) weapon systems
proposals.lexicon_quote: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) / Intel Surv Recon (ISR)
proposals.rationale: The only thing shared with the index row is the bare acronym ISR, which the rubric treats as a weak generic name. The index name is a specific Low Earth Orbit ISR effort under the Tactical Electronic Surveillance System advanced-development line; the announcement buys open-ended 'research, development, test and evaluation support to intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance weapon systems' - a support-services modification with no system, increment or program named.
